# design-intelligence

Context-aware design intelligence for AI coding agents — category playbooks, theme token presets, journey consistency rules, and an auditing CLI.

`design-intelligence` turns the patterns that great products exhibit into
machine-readable rules, tokens, and audits. It classifies the product being
built, selects a direction grounded in category research, generates
consistent screens across the entire user journey with production-grade dark
and light themes, and audits existing apps for visual, motion, accessibility,
and consistency defects.

## Why

- **Anti-slop, not taste.** All models trained on the same UIs produce the
  same outputs — indigo gradients, glass cards, bounce animations. A
  rules-plus-evidence layer (tiered facts: observed / verified / inferred) is
  the only correction that survives long agentic sessions; prompt
  exhortations do not.
- **The whole journey, not one beautiful page.** Stage contracts
  (discovery → landing → signup → onboarding → dashboard → core workflow →
  detail → settings → errors/empty → retention) plus 10 cross-screen
  consistency invariants, so an app stops feeling like five different
  products.
- **Dark-mode excellence as a first-class feature.** The deepest dark-theme
  spec in the corpus: background elevation ladders, border elevation instead
  of shadows, accent lifts, halation and vibration controls — paired-map
  parity enforced for light themes.

## Quick start

```sh
npm i design-intelligence                 # once — adds the `di` CLI to your project
npx di init --name MyApp --category healthcare --install-agents
```

`init` classifies your product (category, audience, stage), writes the Design
Contract to `design/DESIGN.md` with the category's default token preset,
installs token presets, and (with `--install-agents`) installs the
skill into every coding agent dir it creates:

| Agent | Install path |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills` |
| Cursor | `.cursor/skills` |
| Codex | `.codex/skills` |
| OpenCode | `.opencode/skills` |
| Gemini | `.gemini/skills` |

After that, work in your agent session by just asking ("build the settings
page", "make it dark", "audit my UI") — the skill auto-loads from its
frontmatter. Verify what it builds with `npx di audit --dir <folder>` and
`npx di score --dir <folder>`.

### Which category / preset to choose

npx di init --name MyApp --category <category> [--preset <preset>] --install-agents

## CLI (`di`)

Zero runtime dependencies; the binary bundles its own parser. All commands
emit human markdown plus `--json` for CI.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `di init` | Interactive classification → writes `design/DESIGN.md`, installs tokens, optionally installs the skill into a detected agent |
| `di add <target>` | Add a category playbook, checklist, or recipe set into the repo |
| `di tokens emit` | Render a preset as CSS vars, Tailwind `@theme`, or a CSS-in-JS map |
| `di tokens lint` | Scan the repo for hardcoded colors/values outside the token contract |
| `di audit` | Run deterministic detectors over repo CSS/JSX; `--report audit.md` (or any path) writes a scored report; `--json` for CI; `--live` (Playwright screenshot matrix + axe scan) lands in 0.2.x |
| `di doctor` | Environment check: agent detection, token drift, contract age |
| `di score` | Journey consistency score, 0–100 across the 10 invariants |

Exit codes: `0` pass · `1` warnings · `2` failures · `3` runtime/usage error
(bad args, missing files or config).

## Token presets

Presets are installed theme genes, not generated — validation-gated
(`validatePreset` must pass). Each preset defines an OKLCH surface ladder,
border-elevation alphas, accent behavior, status discipline, type rules,
radius family, and a motion duration scale.

| Preset | Cast | Use for | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `graphite-technical` | cool blue-gray | dev tools, dashboards, SaaS, AI products | hue ~265, chroma ≤ 0.02; text like Linear's `#f7f8f8`-on-`#08090a` discipline |
| `warm-charcoal` | warm | fintech, healthcare — calm authority | hue ~50–70, chroma 0.005–0.015; Stripe-adjacent restraint |
| `pure-neutral` | achromatic | docs, editorial, photography | chroma 0; border elevation carries all depth |
| `tinted-statement` | accent-hued | one-brand immersive sites | hue = accent hue, chroma 0.02–0.035; IBM Quantum-style canvas |

Emit them for your stack:

```sh
npx design-intelligence tokens emit --preset graphite-technical --format tailwind
```

## The Design Contract + progressive loading

`init` writes a **Design Contract** — one source of truth in your repo:

```md
product:  Palisade · audience: SMB finance teams · stage: v1 launch
category: fintech-payments
tokens:   warm-charcoal preset
journey:  onboarding → balances → transactions → payouts → settings
signatures: [mono-amount-hero, border-elevation panels]
do_not:   [gradient-CTA, glow-effect, emoji-in-UI, animated-money]
```

Every later generation or audit task must conform to it. The skill loads
progressively to stay sharp and cheap in long sessions:

1. `SKILL.md` — entry point and pipeline (~200 lines).
2. `core/*` — foundations, dark theme, light theme, motion, journey, rules
   (~600 lines). Read every session.
3. **One** category playbook matched to the product — its anti-patterns are
   binding. Loading more than two category files per session is forbidden
   unless you ask.
4. Recipes only for the components actually in play, in the detected stack
   (shadcn/Radix/Chakra/MUI are detected, never replaced).

## Audit + score

`di audit` runs deterministic detectors (slop lexicon + quality rules) over
your repository and writes a scored report; every finding maps to a
suggested fix, not just a flag:

```text
$ npx design-intelligence audit --report
audit: 1 failure, 3 warnings, 27 checks passed (exit code 2)
  FAIL  stateless-button   src/components/CTA.tsx:22 — no hover/focus/disabled styles
        fix: add the 8-state matrix (default/hover/focus/active/selected/disabled/loading/error)
  WARN  shadow-in-dark     src/app/globals.css:41 — box-shadow inside [data-theme="dark"]
        fix: border elevation via --border-* tokens; reserve shadows for the top layer
  WARN  pure-black         src/app/globals.css:12 — #000 canvas
        fix: base token ≥ oklch 0.145 (ladder stop, not pure black)
```

`di score` measures cross-screen consistency (type, color, geometry, states,
icons, motion, voice, responsiveness, roles, journey back-references):

```text
$ npx design-intelligence score
journey consistency: 84/100 (ship bar: 80)
  type ......... 9/10   body 14px consistent across app screens
  color ........ 8/10   accent doubles as decoration on /pricing
  geometry ..... 9/10   token-sourced sidebar/radius stable
  deduction list and per-invariant detail in score.md
```

## Examples

Runnable, dependency-free reference implementations live in `examples/`:

- `examples/dark-dashboard/` — graphite-technical app shell: elevation
  ladder, KPI tiles with sparklines, a state-complete data table, focus
  ring, skeletons, and the full 8-state button matrix.
- `examples/light-landing/` — pure-neutral marketing page: hero formula,

## What ships in v0.1.0

- **Skill bundle** (`skill/`): `SKILL.md` + progressive-loading `core/*`
  (foundations, dark theme, light theme, motion, journey, rules) + 14
  category playbooks + token presets + recipes + checklists (a11y,
  dark-mode, responsive, journey-consistency).
- **Token system**: `validatePreset`-gated YAML presets emitting to CSS
  vars / Tailwind `@theme` / CSS-in-JS, with `tokens lint` enforcement
  (`--lockfile` semantic diff for CI).
- **Journey framework**: universal journey spine, 10-stage contracts, the
  Design Contract, and the 10 consistency invariants behind `di score`.
- **Detector foundation**: deterministic, fix-annotated
  (gradient-CTA, glass-everything, indigo-primary, shadow-in-dark,
  pure-black, stateless-button, mobile-afterthought, and more), each with
  should-fail/should-pass fixtures.
- **Examples, docs, CI**: the two demo pages above, publishing/acceptance
  runbooks, contributor rules, and a two-LTS GitHub Actions workflow.
- **No**: live-render audits and MCP gates (0.2.x, see Roadmap).

# Examples

Two self-contained static reference implementations of the design-intelligence
v0.1.0 contracts. Both are plain HTML files with inline CSS: no build step, no
CDN, no fonts fetched (system font stacks only), no JavaScript required to
open them — double-click or serve them statically.

The corpus reference implementations (Ledgerline, Shipyard, Concierge, Bloom,
Harborview) ship as full-journey apps in a later release; these two pages are
the packaged, dependency-free component+token demonstrations.

## `dark-dashboard/` — graphite-technical

An app-shell demo for the dashboard/dev-tool audience, dark-native per the
deep-dive §6.2 production ladder (values copied exactly, OKLCH included):

- background elevation ladder (base / surface / elevated / sunken) with
  border elevation and alpha borders — no dark drop shadows;
- sidebar shell with grouped nav and active item, collapsing to a top-tab
  bar at ≤768px;
- KPI strip (value + delta + inline SVG sparkline bars) including one
  skeleton-shimmer loading tile;
- a data table with tabular numerals and hover / selected / empty / error
  row states;
- a primary CTA and a visible focus ring (2px + offset + halo alpha);
- an explicit empty-state card stating the next action;
- all 8 interactive states (default, hover, focus, active, selected,
  disabled, loading, error) demonstrated on a `.states-matrix` row;
- responsive grids at 640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 and a
  `prefers-reduced-motion` block.

Footer credit: `tokens: graphite-technical preset v0.1.0`.

## `light-landing/` — pure-neutral light

A marketing demo for the landing/marketing-docs category, light ladder per
the deep-dive §7.1 (off-white canvas — never pure `#ffffff`):

- hero formula (≤9-word headline, one-sentence subhead, primary + secondary
  CTA, framed product visual, one trust line);
- bento grid with exactly two tile sizes, one carrier tile and copy tiles;
- text-only testimonial; pricing with 3 tiers and a "Popular" badge;
- `prefers-color-scheme: dark` auto theming (pure-neutral dark stops) with
  no-flash explicit `data-theme` blocks;
- tabular numerals for prices, all 8 button states on the
  `.states-matrix` row, responsive at 640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280, and a
  `prefers-reduced-motion` block.

Footer credit: `tokens: pure-neutral preset v0.1.0 (light ladder per deep-dive §7.1)`.

# design-intelligence — token presets (`skill/tokens/`)

Installed theme genes for `design-intelligence` v0.1.0. Presets are **installed,
not generated** (deep-dive §13.4) so quality stays central: every emitted value
below is derivable from the four preset files in `presets/`, and every new
preset must pass `validatePreset` with `ok: true` before merge.

## The four shipped presets

| id | cast | use for | radius | accent family |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `graphite-technical` | cool (hue 265, C≤0.02) | dev tools, dashboards (Linear-modeled) | 6px | blue-indigo |
| `warm-charcoal` | warm (hue 60, C 0.006–0.012) | fintech, healthcare | 8px | forest |
| `pure-neutral` | neutral (C=0) | docs, editorial, photography | 10px | slate-blue (restrained) |
| `tinted-statement` | tinted (hue = accent hue, C 0.02–0.035) | one-brand media / portfolio | 12px | vivid violet |

All four ship **both themes** (`dark` + `light`), the same motion budget
(`[80,120,160,240,400,600]`, enter/exit easings, spring 260/26) and a standard
status set (info/success/warning/danger fills + text + alpha borders).

## Resolution model

Tokens resolve in one pass per theme, top-down:

1. **Cast** (`themes.<t>.cast`: hue + chroma) feeds every surface stop.
2. **Ladder** (`themes.<t>.ladder` = 4 lightness values in positional order
   `base → surface → elevated → overlay`) is combined with the cast into
   `oklch(L C H)` strings; `themes.<t>.sunken` supplies the inset well below
   base (`sunken < ladder[0]` is validated). Dark ladder is strictly ascending
   (luminance stacking, §6.2); the light ladder follows the §7.1 convention
   (`surface` is the brightest stop = white cards on an off-white canvas).
3. **Alphas** (`borderAlpha`, `hoverAlpha`, `activeAlpha`) are rendered as
   overlay-color `rgba()` strings. Dark overlays are white; light overlays are
   black (same alphas, inverted direction — see deviations below).
4. **Accent** is a per-theme L-ladder (`value → hover → active`) in oklch.
   `--accent-subtle` = `rgba(r,g,b,α)` where `r,g,b` is the sRGB conversion of
   the theme's accent value and α is the theme's `accent.subtleAlpha`
   (10–14% per §6.4; the conversion is a self-contained OKLab→sRGB transform,
   gamut-clamped when a color leaves sRGB).
5. **Status / type / radius / motion** are theme-invariant: emitted identically
   into both theme blocks. Radius derives `sm = md − 2`, `lg = md + 4`
   (`pill` as given); type derives `small = body − 1` (flat steps per §5.1.3)
   and `display = round(body × scale)`; motion `fast = scale[0]`,
   `base = scale[2]`.

No hardcoded color extras: every color string traces back to the cast, a
ladder value, an alpha, or a status/accent entry in the preset.

## 3-layer architecture recap (§5.2.1 — non-negotiable)

The emitted CSS variables cover **layer 2 (semantic)**:

```
Layer 1  PRIMITIVES  oklch ladder stops in the preset (never used in UI)
Layer 2  SEMANTIC    --bg-* · --text-* · --border-* · --accent-* · --status-*   ← what we emit
Layer 3  COMPONENT   button.primary.bg, input.border.focus … = aliases of layer 2
```

Components must reference layer 2/3 tokens only — the ladder/cast/alpha data
in `themes.*` is *layer 1* and must never appear in component CSS. Light and
dark are one component layer with two token maps, never a rewrite.

node -e "import('design-intelligence/tokens').then(m=>console.log(m.emitCssVars(m.loadPreset('graphite-technical'))))"

# only the dark block ([data-theme="dark"])

### Emitting the CSS output

```js
import { emitCssVars, emitTailwind } from 'design-intelligence/tokens'

const page = emitCssVars(preset)            // ':root { light … }\n\n[data-theme="dark"] { dark … }\n'
const dark = emitCssVars(preset, { theme: 'dark' })  // single [data-theme="dark"] block
const tw   = emitTailwind(preset)           // Tailwind v4 @theme block (colors + radius)
```

`emitCssVars` accepts theme `"both"` (default), `"dark"`, or `"light"`; the
light block is always emitted under `:root`, the dark block under
`[data-theme="dark"]` — theme switching is the attribute, not a rewrite.

### Tailwind v4 / v3 / Radix

- **Tailwind v4** — paste `emitTailwind(preset)` into your global stylesheet;
  classes like `bg-bg-surface`, `text-text-primary`, `border-border-default`,
  `bg-accent`, `rounded-md` resolve from the `--color-*` / `--radius-*` theme
  vars. The block is generated from the **light** theme (`:root` is the v4
  default), with dark mode provided by the emitted `[data-theme="dark"]` vars.
- **Tailwind v3** — v3 has no `@theme`; extend `tailwind.config.js` instead and
  point each semantic key at the CSS var: `colors.bg.base: 'var(--bg-base)'`,
  `colors.accent: 'var(--accent)'`, `borderRadius.md: 'var(--radius-md)'`.
  Keep emitting the CSS vars with `emitCssVars` as run source of truth.
- **Radix / shadcn-style primitives** — never restyle primitive internals; map
  token vars onto the primitive's CSS custom properties
  (`--accent` → `--radix-accent`, popover surface → `--bg-elevated`, tooltip →
  `--bg-overlay`), and keep `color-scheme` in sync with `data-theme` so native
  form controls, scrollbars and autofill follow suit (§6.6). Focus rings use
  `--accent` with a halo alpha (`--accent-subtle`) — never a raw hex.

## Adding a preset

1. Add `skill/tokens/presets/<family>.mjs` with `export default { … }` using
   exactly this shape (deep-dive §13.4 contract):

```js
{
  id, name, summary, cast,
  surface: { ladder: { base, surface, elevated, overlay }, sunken },
  borderAlpha: { subtle, default, emphasis },
  hoverAlpha, activeAlpha,
  accent: { family, hue, chromaRange: [min, max], interactiveLift, brandL, interactiveL, hoverL },
  status: { info: { bg, text, border }, success: { … }, warning: { … }, danger: { … } },
  type: { appPx, scale, trackingRule, monoPx },
  radius: { family, pill },
  motion: { scale: [80,120,160,240,400,600], enter, exit, spring: { stiffness, damping } },
  themes: {
    dark:  { cast: { hue, chroma }, ladder: [4 L values], sunken,
             text: { primary, secondary, muted },
             accent: { value, hover, active, subtleAlpha } },
    light: { …same shape… }
  }
}
```

Schema contract highlights (all enforced by `validatePreset`):

- `id`/`name`/`summary`/`cast` non-empty strings; `themes` map has `dark`+`light`.
- `surface.ladder` strictly ascending; `sunken` below `base`;
  `themes.dark.ladder` must mirror `surface.ladder` exactly.
- `themes.dark.ladder` strictly ascending (luminance stacking); light `ladder`
  values within `(0,1]` with `surface > base` (white cards on off-white).
- Every alpha (`borderAlpha.*`, `hoverAlpha`, `activeAlpha`, `accent.subtleAlpha`)
  within `[0,1]`; `hoverAlpha ≤ activeAlpha`; border alphas ascending.
- Accent ladder rises on dark: `interactiveL ≈ brandL + interactiveLift` (±0.015)
  and `hoverL > interactiveL`; `chromaRange` is `[min,max]` with
  `0 ≤ min < max ≤ 0.4`.
- `motion.scale` is an exact, strictly ascending 6-number array.
- Text/accent/status colors are oklch strings (status may carry an alpha).

2. Register it in the `REGISTRY` array in `skill/tokens/index.mjs`.
3. Run `npx vitest run tests/tokens.test.mjs` — **validation is mandatory**:
   `validatePreset` must return `ok: true` for every shipped preset or CI fails.
   Fix the values, never the validator.
4. Regenerate previews (both-theme blocks per preset):

```sh

import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
mkdirSync('skill/tokens/preview', { recursive: true });
for (const { id } of listPresets())
  writeFileSync('skill/tokens/preview/' + id + '.css',

```

## Known deviations (documented decisions)

- **Light-theme overlays are black, not white.** The shared contract reads
  "rgba white overlays for hover/active/borders"; dark emits
  `rgba(255,255,255,α)` exactly as written. For the light theme the same alphas
  are applied in the opposite direction (`rgba(0,0,0,α)`), because white
  overlays on a `1.0` white surface are invisible and §7.1/§5.4 require
  burn-darker hairlines and 2–4% tints on light.
- **`emitTailwind` renders the light theme.** `@theme` is Tailwind's root-level
  (light-default) token source, matching `emitCssVars`' `:root = light`
  convention; dark stays in the `[data-theme="dark"]` CSS-vars block which the
  `@theme` vars can reference or be replaced by.
- **Status/status pairs are dark-first.** Per the assignment ("bg subtle L
  .3x, alpha-ish + text bright") the status triple is emitted identically in
  both theme blocks; apps needing dark-text statuses on light should alias
  layer-3 component tokens over them per §5.2.1.
- **Light `--bg-elevated`/`--bg-overlay` follow the assignment's §7.1-anchored
  pale stops (0.97/0.99)** rather than pure white, per the assigned light
  ladder convention.

- Body text target AAA (≥7:1) on long-read surfaces; secondary text holds ≥8:1, muted ≥5:1 — measured against the light ladder.
- Charts: goal line dashed + solid trend + point markers (survive grayscale), ≥12px mono labels, twin data table for the same values.
- Training-free semantics: `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`, `aria-current="step"`/`"page"`, `role="status"`/`aria-live` toasts and refill status, `role="alert"` errors with actionable human wording (e.g. "Pick a time to continue"), skip link first, one `h1` per page, landmark + heading order kept, tab order never reordered.

# Publishing design-intelligence

Step-by-step runbook for publishing the npm package. Do this only after the
release checklist in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (semver version bump, changelog entry,
green `npm test`) is complete.

## 0. Preconditions

- Node >= 18.17 (package `engines` requirement).
- You have an npm account with 2FA enabled (npm enforces OTP on publish for
  maintained packages).
- `package.json` `files` whitelist is final: `bin/`, `cli/`, `skill/`,
  `audit/`, `docs/`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`. Nothing else ships.
- Clean working tree (no uncommitted corpus/content changes inside
  `skill/`, `audit/`, or `cli/`).

## 1. Authenticate with npm

```sh
npm login            # opens browser flow; type 2FA/device code when prompted
npm whoami           # must print your username — if it errors, re-run login
```

`npm whoami` failures are usually a stale token: re-run `npm login`, or check
`~/.npmrc` for an old `_authToken` pointing at a revoked account.

## 2. Sanity-check the package name

- Current name: `design-intelligence` (unscoped). Name rules that matter:
  - lowercase, no spaces; npm package names cannot contain
    uppercase characters, and new package names cannot contain ambiguous
    lookalike combinations for security (e.g., uppercase `L` casing blocks);
  - cannot match the name of a core Node module;
  - if the name were ever squatted/taken, fall back to a scope and keep the
    CLI intact — the deep-dive §13.2 already reserves scoped alternatives:
    `@di/skill` or, failing that, `@design-intelligence/skill`. A scope
    change means republishing `package.json` `name` and updating install
    examples in the README (`npx <new-name> init`), nothing else: the
    exports map, bin name (`di`), and skill paths are name-independent.
- Check availability/current state before publish:

```sh
npm view design-intelligence        # 404 = available; prints manifest if taken
```

## 3. Dry-run: inspect the payload

```sh
npm pack --dry-run                  # prints the in-process packaged file list
# or write the tarball to an explicit directory:
npm pack --pack-destination ../release-artifacts
```

- `npm pack --dry-run` versus `--pack-destination`: `--dry-run` gives you the
  file listing that `npm publish` would upload without writing a tarball;
  `--pack-destination <dir>` writes the real tarball there. Use a dry run to
  verify no secrets, `node_modules`, or drafts leak into the tarball.

## 4. Publish (2FA / OTP)

```sh
npm publish --access public
```

- The CLI will prompt `[npm] Enter OTP:` — type the code from your authenticator.
- `--access public` is mandatory for scoped (`@di/...`) variants and harmless
  for the unscoped name.
- Never use `npm publish --force`; if the publish aborts with EOTP/E2FA,
  re-run within the OTP validity window.

## 5. Post-publish verification

```sh
npm view design-intelligence                    # remote manifest, version, dist-tags
npm view design-intelligence dist-tags --json   # latest should point here
npx design-intelligence@latest doctor           # installs fresh + runs CLI end-to-end
```

Verify the version and files:

```sh
npx design-intelligence --version 2>/dev/null || npx design-intelligence doctor
```

`doctor` should report agent detection and no token drift. If the freshly
installed CLI fails, `npm uninstall -g design-intelligence` locally, fix, bump
a patch version, and republish (see gotchas below — same version is
immutable).

## 6. Post-publish steps (GitHub release)

1. Tag the exact commit: `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "vX.Y.Z" && git push origin vX.Y.Z`.
2. Create the GitHub release from the tag; paste the `CHANGELOG.md` section
   for this version as the release body.
3. Attach the tarball from step 3 if you want an offline artifact: the file
   produced by `npm pack --pack-destination ../release-artifacts`
   (`design-intelligence-X.Y.Z.tgz`).
4. Update the README symlink/badge reality only if the install command
   changed.

## Gotchas

- **Publishing is immutable.** You cannot re-publish the same
  name+version. `npm deprecate design-intelligence@X` marks it; a fix needs a
  new patch version.
- **Version bump before every publish.** `npm version patch|minor|major`
  (creates a commit + tag) or hand-edit `package.json` and the CHANGELOG
  together. A stale `npm cache` can serve old manifests after a fresh
  publish: see next item.
- **Cache confusion (404 version not found right after publish).** If the
  just-published version is not yet visible locally, clean the cache:
  `npm cache clean --force`, then re-run `npm view` / `npx design-intelligence@latest doctor`.
  The `latest` dist-tag can lag a few seconds in the registry CDN.
- **Lockfile vs publish:** `npm install` locally before `npm pack` so the
  `package-lock.json` reflects the installed dependency graph (dev deps never
  ship under the `files` whitelist, but a corrupt install can break
  pre-publish checks).
- **Scoped fallback:** if `design-intelligence` is unavailable, publish as
  `@di/skill` (deep-dive §13.2 precedent) with `--access public`, and add
  `design-intelligence` as a keyword/description alias so search still finds it.
- **Do not publish from a modified corpus branch.** The skill bundle is the
  content contract; publishing divergent corpus versions without a
  changelog entry breaks agents that pin versions.

# Dark theme system

Flagship spec: OKLCH elevation ladder, binding rules, palettes, accent discipline, component treatments, theme switching, and the 9 deadly sins. ✅ Dark-native categories (dev tools, AI, dashboards, fintech ops, analytics) build this first.

## 1. Why "inverted light mode" fails ✅

Light hierarchy is simulated with an overhead light source (shadows). In dark mode that metaphor collapses — dark shadows on dark shapes are invisible. ✅ Verified across Material Design 3, Radix themes, and Linear teardowns. Pure `#000` + pure `#fff` reading also hurts (halation; astigmatism is worse on dark) — hence the off-white text cap below.

## 2. Elevation ladder (canonical CSS) ✅

Production ladder — 7 tokens, **ΔL ≈ +0.035–0.05 per step**, cool hue cast:

```css
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --bg-base:         oklch(0.145 0.012 265);    /* app canvas */
  --bg-surface:      oklch(0.180 0.012 265);    /* cards, panels */
  --bg-elevated:     oklch(0.215 0.012 265);    /* dropdowns, popovers */
  --bg-overlay:      oklch(0.245 0.012 265);    /* modals, tooltips, toasts */
  --bg-sunken:       oklch(0.115 0.012 265);    /* wells: code blocks, inputs in cards */
  --bg-hover:        rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05);
  --bg-active:       rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
  --border-subtle:   rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);
  --border-default:  rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.10);
  --border-emphasis: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16);
  --text-primary:    oklch(0.93 0.01 265);      /* ~#f7f8f8-class, never #fff */
  --text-secondary:  oklch(0.65 0.012 265);
}
```

Verified anchors for calibration: Linear `#08090a → #0f1011 → #191a1b → #28282c`; Material stop ladder `#121212 → +5% → +7% → +8%…+11%`. ✅

## 3. Ten binding rules ✅💡

1. **Elevation = surface + border, never shadow.** Every elevated surface carries a visible 1px border (`--border-*` alphas above). Shadows are for the top layer only (rule 6).
2. **Sunken wells exist:** code blocks, inputs-in-cards, logs go *down* to `--bg-sunken` (0.115), not up. Amateur dark apps forget inset surfaces.
3. **Small controls may sit opposite the ladder** (inset rule): minor buttons look right slightly darker than their surface; primary CTAs use light fill or accent fill.
4. **Hover grows > selected:** hover lifts `+0.02L` (the `--bg-hover` 5% overlay); selected = **accent-subtle at 10–14% alpha**, never a flat accent fill row.
5. **z-index correlates with surface level:** base(0) < surface(10) < popover(20) < overlay(30). Breaking the correlation reads as flicker.
6. **Top-layer ambient shadow only:** `0 24px 48px -12px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5)` allowed on modals solely as a depth hint.
7. **Text never pure white:** cap on-base contrast ≤ ~16:1; use the `--text-primary` above. Halation is a defect, not a vibe.
8. **Desaturate saturated colors** −10–20% chroma vs light mode; status colors get dim fills + bright text variants (§5).
9. **Zero component conditionals on theme** — token mapping only; ship dark without light leftovers (tooltips, autofill flash, scrollbars, selection color).
10. **Floating panels get the "top-edge light" trick:** 1px top border at white/8% simulates the light source on modals/popovers/command palettes.

## 4. Four palette archetypes 💡

| Archetype | Cast | Use for | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Graphite** | cool blue-gray, hue ~265, C ≤ 0.02 | dev tools, dashboards | Linear, Vercel |
| **Pure neutral** | C = 0 gray | docs, editorial, photography | Vercel/Geist |
| **Warm charcoal** | hue ~50–70, C 0.005–0.015 | fintech, healthcare (calmer) | Stripe-adjacent |
| **Tinted statement** | hue = accent hue, C 0.02–0.035 | one-brand immersive sites | IBM Quantum, Unfair |

## 5. Accents & semantics ✅💡

- **Accent brightness rises in dark mode.** ✅ Verified Linear ladder: brand `#5e6ad2` → interactive `#7170ff` → hover `#828fff`. The brand color alone reads as mud on `#08090a`.
- **Accent-subtle** = accent at 10–14% alpha for selected/active backgrounds; **accent text** = lighten until ≥5.0:1 on base.
- **Status discipline:** dimmable fills with bright text versions. Example success: fill `oklch(0.35 0.1 150)`, text `oklch(0.75 0.15 150)`, border at 20% alpha. Green is for status only, never decoration.
- **Data viz:** ≤7 categorical hues; on dark shift the set toward cyan/magenta/yellow; monotone ramps run base→bright; gridlines at white/6%.

## 6. Component treatments 💡

| Component | Light habit | Dark directive |
|---|---|---|
| Cards | shadow | border + surface step; inner content on sunken wells |
| Tables | row hover tint | hover white/4%; header on surface; sticky header border white/10 |
| Inputs | white fill | sunken fill; border white/10 → focus accent + 50% halo |
| Modals | shadowed sheet | overlay token bg + dim scrim `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6)` + top-edge light (rule 10) |
| Tooltips | dark tooltip | invert the inversion: **light tooltip `oklch(0.92 …)`, dark text** |
| Code blocks | gray bg | sunken well + syntax in the 500–600 range; never pure neon |
| Charts | colorful | gridline white/6%; series = accent family + 0/15° hue offsets; sparklines 1.5px |
| Glow/scrim | decorative | no glows by default; a glow must be motivated (hero art only), radius 3× element, ≤8% alpha |
| Images | as-is | dim −15–25% or dark duotone; hairline border |

## 7. Theme switching ✅

- Token-mapping only; zero component conditionals on theme.
- Animate color tokens over 150–200ms **but** respect `prefers-reduced-motion` / `prefers-reduced-transparency` → instant switch.
- Anti-flash trick: gate the transition behind a `.theme-transition` class applied for one frame, then removed — avoids a systemic color flash on load.
- Persist choice; default to `prefers-color-scheme`; **pre-hydration inline script** prevents FOUC:

```html
<script>
  document.documentElement.dataset.theme =
    localStorage.theme ?? (matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches ? "dark" : "light");
</script>
```

- Support forced exceptions per region: `data-theme="light"` on an embedded component (e.g., a chart destined for export).
- 💡 Demo device: the vibrant.design "comparison slider" is the canonical way to demo/QA theme quality.

## 8. The 9 deadly sins ✅

1. Pure black `#000` canvas (breaks hierarchy + ghosting; media-entertainment exempt).
2. Elevation by shadow instead of surface + border.
3. All surfaces identical (flat mud) or over-contrasted steps (zebra).
4. Excessive glow/neon — the "AI dashboard from hell".
5. Text pure white ≥16:1 → halation.
6. Saturated colors unreduced → vibration everywhere.
7. Light leftovers: white tooltips, default autofill flash, unstyled scrollbar, wrong selection color.
8. Images brighter than their chrome or invisible (no hairline border).
9. Focus rings invisible (dark-on-dark) — every focusable renders ≥3:1.

# Journey & screen consistency framework

The answer to "a beautiful landing page isn't enough if the dashboard feels like a different product": the universal journey spine, the DESIGN.md contract (what `di init` writes), 10 stage contracts, and the 10 consistency invariants scored by `di score`. ✅💡

## 1. Journey spine 💡✅

```text
Discovery → Landing → Signup → Onboarding → Dashboard → Core Workflow
          → Detail Views → Settings → Errors / Empty / Success → Retention
```

Each stage emits a **screen contract**: purpose, primary action, system needs, component inventory, state list, and inherited consistency rules. Before styling any screen, find its stage below and honor the primary action and known risks.

## 2. The Design Contract (`design/DESIGN.md`) 💡

Single source of truth written at `npx design-intelligence init`. Manual template — **field names must match the CLI exactly**:

````md
# DESIGN.md (generated)

name:         {name}
category:     {category}          <!-- one of the 14 playbooks -->
audience:     {audience}
stage:        {stage}             <!-- pre-launch | v1 | mature -->
personality:  {personality}       <!-- 2–3 traits, e.g. [calm-authority, precision] -->
tokens:       {preset}            <!-- graphite-technical | warm-charcoal | pure-neutral | tinted-statement -->
type:         {type}              <!-- display + body + mono + scale decisions -->
journey:      {journey}           <!-- ordered stages this product actually ships -->
signatures:   {signatures}        <!-- the ONE signature move + surface list -->
voice:        {voice}             <!-- error toasts, empty states, settings labels share it -->
do_not:       {do_not}            <!-- forbidden patterns for THIS product -->
````

Worked example (from the report): fintech "Palisade" — `warm-charcoal` preset, Söhne + Berkeley Mono numerals, journey `onboarding → balances → transactions → payouts → settings`, signatures `[mono-amount-hero, border-elevation panels]`, voice "plain, precise, never cute about money", `do_not: [gradient-CTA, glow-effect, emoji-in-UI, animated-money]`.

Every subsequent generation/audit task re-states contract identity or defers to it; agents re-read only diffs (progressive loading).

## 3. Stage contracts (10) ✅

| Stage | Purpose | Primary action | Signature risks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discovery | qualify | understand in 5s | overdesign vs message clarity |
| Landing | convert (1 CTA) | start / signup | generic AI-slop hero; 3 competing CTAs |
| Signup | reduce friction | one field before password | asking company size too early; no SSO |
| Onboarding | reach first value | import / connect / **skip** | 7-step tours; empty-dashboard terror; no skip |
| Dashboard | answer "am I OK?" | 1 answer above fold | 12 KPI tiles = none chosen; spinner on load |
| Core workflow | momentum | complete in ≤3 decisions | modal-nesting; dead ends |
| Detail | context + next action | drill or return | breadcrumb loss; no next/prev |
| Settings | self-serve confidence | account to outcome | destructive actions styled normal |
| Errors/Empty | recover | next step stated | dead 404s; empty = blank panel |
| Retention | return value | digest / upgrade | streak-guilt; paywall ambush |

## 4. The 10 consistency invariants ✅💡 (the `score` command audits these)

1. **Type:** identical app-body px across dashboard/detail/settings tables; heading ramp shared with marketing but *scaled down*; marketing-only fonts never cross into the app.
2. **Accent meaning:** the accent means "interactive" on every screen — never decoration on landing but status on dashboard.
3. **Geometry:** sidebar width, content max-width, row height, card radius, button height are identical token values everywhere (CSS-diff auditable).
4. **States:** every list/table/modal implements all 8 states (default, hover, focus-visible, active/pressed, selected, disabled, loading, error) — in both themes.
5. **Icons:** one family, one stroke weight; illustrations from one library; avatar shape = the product's radius family.
6. **Motion:** one duration scale + one easing family product-wide; page transitions identical in both directions.
7. **Voice:** error toasts, empty states, and settings labels share the contract voice (e.g., fintech: "money never jokes").
8. **Responsiveness:** navigation shifts to the same pattern at the same breakpoint app-wide.
9. **Roles:** RBAC differences render as *visibility* (disabled/hidden fields), never as a different visual language per role.
10. **Journey back-references:** completing onboarding removes the dashboard's empty state and states what's next — earlier work is carried forward, never reset to zero.

# Light theme system

Light-mode ladder, shadow tiers, and the parity rules that keep light + dark feeling like one product. ✅ Every ship needs both — a dark-only app without a light map halves its audience and fails the paired-map audit.

## 1. Canonical ladder (CSS) ✅

```css
:root[data-theme="light"] {
  --bg-base:         oklch(0.985 0.003 265);   /* off-white canvas — never #fff for the canvas */
  --bg-surface:      oklch(1.000 0 0);         /* cards white */
  --bg-elevated:     oklch(1.000 0 0);         /* popovers: separation via shadow */
  --bg-overlay:      oklch(1.000 0 0);         /* modals: shadow does the work */
  --bg-sunken:       oklch(0.965 0.004 265);   /* inputs, wells */
  --bg-hover:        oklch(0.975 0.004 265);   /* light hover = 2–4% bg tint */
  --bg-active:       oklch(0.962 0.004 265);
  --border-subtle:   oklch(0.92 0.005 265);
  --border-default:  oklch(0.88 0.006 265);
  --border-emphasis: oklch(0.80 0.008 265);
  --text-primary:    oklch(0.20 0.01 265);     /* never #000 */
  --text-secondary:  oklch(0.45 0.01 265);
}
```

Four shadow tiers (light elevation = shadow):

```css
--shadow-xs: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05);
--shadow-sm: 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.07), 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05);
--shadow-md: 0 4px 12px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.08);
--shadow-lg: 0 16px 48px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.14);   /* modals */
```

💡 Linear uses these inversions deliberately: `#f7f8f8` text on the dark side becomes near-black-but-not `#000` here — text is never absolute black on light.

## 2. Paired-map parity rules ✅

1. **Same token names in both themes.** Light and dark are two maps over identical component layers — a component that only reads `--border-default` works everywhere. If a token exists in one theme and not the other, the map is broken.
2. **Accent shifts for contrast.** Light mode darkens/derives chroma-reduced accent so white-on-accent text holds ≥4.5:1; dark mode needs the brightened interactive + hover variants instead (Linear: `#5e6ad2` → `#7170ff` → `#828fff`). Never reuse the dark accent byte-for-byte on light.
3. **No pure-black text, no pure-white canvas.** Halation has a light-mode cousin: #fff canvas under tinted accents looks dead — hence `oklch(0.985 0.003 265)`.
4. **Shadows never appear in dark; borders carry all depth.** The reverse is also rule-bound: don't rely on shadow alone for nested depth in light mode — layer `--border-subtle` + `--bg-sunken` for in-card insets, shadows for floaters.
5. **Hover/active map to tint tokens** (`--bg-hover`, `--bg-active`), not ad-hoc `bg-neutral-50` utilities.

## 3. Acceptance ritual ✅

- Audit = render the **component matrix in both themes and diff *states*, not just resting UI** — hover/selected/disabled/loading included.
- The vibrant.design "light/dark comparison slider" is the canonical review device; CI can reproduce it via screenshot matrix (375/768/1440 × theme × 8 states, `audit --live` from 0.2.x).
- 💡 Contrast never recomputed per-element ad hoc — token-level fixes only (`di tokens emit` regenerates both maps).

# Motion & interaction engineering

Motion is a budget, not a garnish. One duration scale + one easing family per product, a decision table for when to animate, a tool-selection matrix, and hard accessibility requirements. ✅ Stripe 100ms micro standard; saas-dark corpus 150ms normal; GPU-only rule.

## 1. Budgets 💡

```text
Per screen:   ≤2 entrance animations · ≤3 simultaneous transitions · 0 ambient loops
              (ambient loop only when the loop IS the product — e.g., an AI waiting state)
Per journey:  entrances identical everywhere; durations from one scale (nothing else):
              80 · 120 · 160 · 240 · 400 · 600 (ms)
```

## 2. Easing tokens (one family per product) ✅

```text
exit    cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 1, 1)      fast-in
enter   cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1) decelerate-out
spring  { stiffness: 260, damping: 26 } (Framer/Motion — physical; position/size only)
```

- **Exits = 60–70% of enter duration.**
- Springs only for transform/opacity (GPU-only rule); never spring a color, text, or layout prop that reflows.
- Streamed content is linear; a line settles cubic-out after stream end.

## 3. When to animate ✅💡

| Animate when… | Never animate when… |
|---|---|
| a state change is otherwise invisible (expand, reveal, swap) | text is being read; text moves >2 lines |
| spatial continuity helps (drawer ↔ anchor element) | data updates every frame (streams/tickers — count-up one-shot excepted) |
| feedback confirms (like, copied, saved) | the user is waiting (loading hides time ⇒ skeletons instead) |
| it establishes the brand once per session | it would repeat >2× per session identically |
| gesture-following (drag/swipe must track 1:1) | an exit delays the user's next target |

## 4. Implementation matrix ✅

| Need | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| UI micro-states, list FLIP | CSS transitions + WAAPI | cheapest; tokens live in CSS vars |
| Orchestrated entrances, layout, scroll-linked | Motion for React (Framer) | `whileInView` once; springs for layout; `AnimatePresence` for exits |
| Scroll narratives, timelines | GSAP + ScrollTrigger | CSS-variable bridge to tokens; portfolio-scale pages |
| Vector/icon morphs, data-viz entrances | WAAPI/JS or Motion — **not SMIL** | path morph via flubber; SMIL deprecated |
| Launch films, OG motion | Remotion | render → webm/mp4 + poster fallback |
| Shader/3D moments | Three.js / R3F | <200KB gzip · 60fps mid-tier phones · DPR cap 1.5 · `prefers-reduced-motion` = **hard off** |
| Streaming AI UI | Motion + custom rAF | chunk-reveal, not per-char tween (see recipes/motion-kit) |

Copy-paste snippets for the common cases live in [../recipes/react-tailwind-shadcn/motion-kit.md](../recipes/react-tailwind-shadcn/motion-kit.md).

## 5. Accessibility requirements ✅ (all tools)

- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` = global kill → crossfade fallback (duration 0 — instant state swap, no movement).
- No autoplaying audio; motion respects WCAG 2.2 seizure thresholds (nothing flashes >3×/s).
- Carousels/billboards pause on hover and hide when offscreen.
- Every animated control is keyboard-operable; motion never replaces a legible state (e.g., a toast entering is also announced).

## 6. Anti-pattern reel ✅💡

Parallax over body text · scroll-jacking (full-page hijack) · spinners shown >400ms (use skeletons) · hover-lift + glow + tilt trifecta · cards whose padding morphs · entrance-delay chains accumulating >600ms · ambient loops that aren't the product.

# Design rules knowledge base

Ordered principles, the Do/Don't lists, and the AI-slop lexicon that `di audit` enforces. 💡✅ Slop ids marked **[detected]** map to deterministic CLI detectors where implementable.

## 1. Principles, ordered 💡

1. **Context beats taste.** Category → direction; never one aesthetic everywhere.
2. **Honesty beats polish.** Real states, real data, no fake counters.
3. **Consistency compounds.** Tokens and invariants first; delight second.
4. **Density with dignity.** Information design is the product UI for dense apps.
5. **One signature move per product.** Own it across all surfaces.
6. **Accessibility is layout.** Contrast/order/focus are structural, not cosmetic.
7. **Motion with purpose.** State > decoration, always.
8. **Defaults do the heavy lifting.** Choosing a default IS the design decision.

## 2. Do list (15) ✅💡

1. Ship every interactive element with the 8 states (both themes).
2. All colors via semantic tokens in both themes — no hex in components.
3. Dark = border elevation; shadows only top-layer ambient hint.
4. Table numerals tabular and right-aligned.
5. Focus-visible ring ≥3:1, 2px + 2px offset; never `outline:none` without replacement.
6. Skeletons for >300ms loads; spinners only <300ms or genuinely uncertain.
7. Empty states state the next action; never blame the user.
8. Errors human + specific + recovery path; never raw codes in user UI.
9. One accent; status colors a separate discipline.
10. Hit targets ≥44px mobile / 24px pointer-exact.
11. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`, `prefers-contrast`, `forced-colors`.
12. WCAG AA everywhere; AAA on text-dense reading surfaces.
13. In-product copy follows the contract voice.
14. Test at 375 / 768 / 1440 always; RTL pass occasionally.
15. Stakes grow with risk: destructive = red + typed confirmation + undo ≤5s where possible.

## 3. Don't list (10) ✅💡

1. Don't nest modals; use drawers/steppers.
2. Don't center everything; left-align data.
3. Don't animate money, medical, or legal text.
4. Don't use gradient CTAs or glow as hierarchy.
5. Don't ship dark mode with the light leftovers (tooltips, autofill, scrollbars, selection).
6. Don't put the placeholder-empty main content behind a login wall (empty trapdoor).
7. Don't mix icon families or borrow brand marks.
8. Don't lock scroll with body-overflow hacks; use proper scroll lock.
9. Don't let marketing assets dictate app typography.
10. Don't create information-asymmetry games (hidden pricing, fees animated away).
